name.text: Modelling temperature with a cosine function

questiontext.text:
The temperature in a coastal town can be modelled by the function:

\(T(t)={@D@}+{@A@}\cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{24}(t-{@C@})\right)\)

where \(T(t)\) is the temperature in degrees Celsius and \(t\) is the number of hours after midnight.

The graph below represents the temperature throughout a 24-hour period.

Using the model and the graph, determine the following:

[[jsxgraph height='400px' width='600px']] /* Retrieve values from STACK */ var amplitude = {#A#}; var midline = {#D#}; var period = {#P#}; var maximumTime = {#C#}; /* Set the vertical graph limits */ var ymin = midline - amplitude - 2; var ymax = midline + amplitude + 2; /* Initialise the board */ var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [0, ymax, period, ymin], axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, keepaspectratio: false }); /* Define the temperature function directly in JavaScript */ var temperature = function(t) { return midline + amplitude * Math.cos((2 * Math.PI / period) * (t - maximumTime)); }; /* Draw the temperature graph */ board.create('functiongraph', [temperature, 0, period], { strokeColor: 'blue', strokeWidth: 3 }); /* Add graph labels */ board.create('text', [18, ymin + 0.5, 'Time (hours)'], { fixed: true, fontSize: 14 }); board.create('text', [0.5, ymax - 0.5, 'Temperature (°C)'], { fixed: true, fontSize: 14 }); board.update(); [[/jsxgraph]]

(a) Identify the amplitude of the temperature variation.

[[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]]

(b) Identify the midline temperature.

[[input:ans2]]

[[validation:ans2]]

(c) Determine the period of the temperature cycle, in hours.

[[input:ans3]]

[[validation:ans3]]

(d) Determine the time at which the daily maximum temperature occurs. Give your answer as the number of hours after midnight.

[[input:ans4]]

[[validation:ans4]][[feedback:prt1]]

Instructions: Give numerical answers. Include the appropriate units where requested.

generalfeedback.text:
Woked solution

We are given the temperature model:

\(T(t)={@D@}+{@A@}\cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{24}(t-{@C@})\right)\)

where \(T(t)\) is the temperature in degrees Celsius and \(t\) is the number of hours after midnight.

(a) Finding the amplitude

A cosine function in the form \(T(t)=D+A\cos(B(t-C))\) has an amplitude equal to the absolute value of the coefficient of the cosine function.

\(\text{Amplitude}=|A|={@A@}\)

Therefore, the amplitude is: \(\boxed{{@ta1@}^\circ\text{C}}\)

(b) Finding the midline temperature

The midline is determined by the constant term outside the cosine function.

\(\text{Midline}: T=D\)

Substituting the given value: \(T={@D@}\)

Therefore, the midline temperature is: \(\boxed{{@ta2@}^\circ\text{C}}\)

(c) Finding the period

The period of a cosine function of the form \(T(t)=D+A\cos(B(t-C))\) is given by:

\(\text{Period}=\dfrac{2\pi}{|B|}\)

In this question: \(B=\dfrac{2\pi}{24}\)

Hence:

\(\text{Period}=\dfrac{2\pi}{2\pi/24}\)

\(\text{Period}=24\)

Therefore, the temperature cycle has a period of: \(\boxed{{@ta3@}\text{ hours}}\)

(d) Finding the time of maximum temperature

The maximum value of the cosine function is \(1\). Therefore, the temperature reaches its maximum when:

\(\cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{24}(t-{@C@})\right)=1\)

For the maximum in the daily cycle, the angle inside the cosine function is zero:

\(\dfrac{2\pi}{24}(t-{@C@})=0\)

Multiplying both sides by \(\dfrac{24}{2\pi}\):

\(t-{@C@}=0\)

Therefore:

\(t={@C@}\)

Since \(t\) represents the number of hours after midnight, the maximum temperature occurs at:

\(\boxed{{@ta4@}\text{ hours after midnight}}\)

This corresponds to \({@ta4@}:00\) on a 24-hour clock.
